label: batch-10
tail:
**Batch 10 is authored:** 8 A items and 5 B examples, with frontmatter-only pages, manifest, proof contracts, coverage, cross-batch evidence, notes, and Step 1 readiness records. Twelve items are marked ready; `thm-ip-sparse-detection-regime-split` is escalated.

The sparse theorem keeps its full claim. Its local proof establishes lower bounds in both regimes and the \(\lambda\le0\) rate upper bound, but not the \(\lambda>0\) consistency upper bound or the sharp error formulas. The 2012 article states Theorem 4.7 but omits its proof and refers to the 2003 book; six retrieval attempts did not recover that proof. The source remains an owner escalation, not a documented drop. [2012 article](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.1853) · [2003 book record](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-21580-8)

**Checks:** proof layout passed for 13 items (49 steps); precheck passed for all 12 proof-bearing items; strict contracts, citation fidelity, rendering, content policy, and scoped dependency checks passed. Source fetch verified 3 of 4 sources; the fourth is the unresolved book.

The run remains held at `1-scaffold` (46/109 covered). The full readiness check is still open, and the run-wide dependency check encounters an unrelated malformed item owned outside this batch. I left published content, shared plans, engine state, and verdicts untouched. The readiness records are author records, not independent approval.
